Birth Control mode is for users on Birth Control. It gives you the option of always using a default cycle to calculate your next period. To set this up, if you are on Birth Control Pills, count how many pills you have including placebos, then set your default cycle for that length of days. For example, if you have 28 pills, set your default cycle to 28 day. You can also set custom notifications reminders and log skipped periods. Skipped periods can be entered from your Period Log.

"*Period Tracker ovulation and fertility forecasts may not be accurate and should not be used to prevent unwanted pregnancy. Forecast accuracy depends on a number of factors including how regular one's cycle length is, when one actually ovulates during the cycle, and how many periods have been logged in the app. Anxiety, stress, diet, nutrition, exercise, environment, medications, age and other factors can also affect one's cycle from month to month."

"Period Tracker normally predicts your next period start date using your average cycle length. For example, if your average cycle length is 28 days, Period Tracker will predict your next period as coming 28 days after the start of your last period.
Predict Periods Using Luteal Length overrides this method of predicting of your next period once Period Tracker has detected that you've ovulated. Once ovulation is detected via the fertility notes that you've inputted, instead of continuing to use your average cycle, it will now predict your next period start date using your ovulation + luteal length. Your luteal length is the number of days that typically pass between your ovulation day and the start of your next period. Using this method once ovulation is detected will likely make your predicted period start date more accurate since luteal length for most women is fairly constant.
By default, Period Tracker sets your luteal length as 14 days. However, you can change your luteal length by going to your app's Settings/General/Ovulation page. Period Tracker will also change your luteal length to more accurately determine your luteal length by using your inputted fertility notes once you have inputted fertility notes for at least one cycle."

Artificial insemination (AI) is one of the simplest of the assisted reproduction methods. AI uses a catheter inserted into your vagina to gently deposit sperm just outside of or within your cervix. Your chances of conception is highest when this is done on your Peak Day.

"BBT or Basal Body Temperature is your body’s resting temperature. Right after you ovulate, your body’s BBT spikes due to an increase in the hormone progesterone in your body. If you see a sudden spike in your body’s BBT, it means that you likely ovulated the day before. After your temperature spike, continue to take your temperature to confirm that your temperatures stay elevated.
To take your BBT, take your temperature first thing when you wake up in the morning. Try to take your temperature at the same time every morning and make sure not to get up or move too much prior to taking your temperature. Your Period Tracker Advanced Fertility Chart will draw a vertical line on your ovulation day based on your BBT inputs."

"Your cervix produces fertile cervical mucus or CM leading up to and on your ovulation day. Fertile cervical mucus is creamy, watery, or the consistency of an egg white. To get pregnant, you will want to have intercourse when you notice watery or egg white cervical mucus as these are the most fertile types of CM. Non fertile cervical mucus is either dry or sticky.
To check your CM, wipe a tissue across the back of the opening of your vagina. Notice the consistency of the CM and take note of it in Period Tracker. Your Advanced Fertility Chart will color the days you have fertile CM in green."

"Your physical cervix changed leading up to ovulation. Your cervical opening is generally low, closed and firm making it difficult for sperm to pass through your cervix into the rest of your uterus. However, from the end of your period to your ovulation, your cervix will gradually become higher, more open, and soft making it easier for sperm to enter. Right after ovulation, your cervix will abruptly return to its low, closed, firm position again.
To check your cervix, squat on the floor or put one leg on a chair and insert your finger into your vagina. When your cervix is closed, firm and low, it will feel like the tip of a nose. As your cervix opens, softens, and gets higher, you should be able to notice the change. Your Advanced Fertility Chart will color the days your cervix indicates that you are fertile in green."

"Ferning works by monitoring your morning saliva under a ferning microscope. During the first part of your cycle, estrogen in your body increasingly builds up which ultimately causes your LH surge and ovulation. The peaking of estrogen in your body also causes your saliva to have an increase in sodium. The sodium in your saliva in turn changes the structure of your saliva which can be observed under a microscope. So by observing your saliva, when you see your saliva change, you can know that your estrogen is at a very high level which means that you can expect ovulation to happen within 1–2 days.
To test, collect a bit of the saliva from under your tongue and put it on the surface of the lens of your microscope. Make sure that you take the sample before eating or drinking anything. Then let the sample dry for 5 minutes before observing. You should be able to see if your sample has no, partial, or full ferning.
Here is a link to purchase a ferning microscope: http://www.amazon.com/Fairhaven–Fertile–Focus–Ovulation–Microscope/dp/B000S2O1CI/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&qid=1392857312&sr=8–1&keywords=ferning"

"The Clearblue Fertility Monitor is a small handheld device that works by analyzing the estrogen and LH in your urine. It can alert you of the 1–5 highly fertile days leading up to your ovulation as well as pinpoint the two peak days of your fertility. To use it, you will need to the actual monitor and the fertility test that you attach to the monitor. On the first day of your period, press the M button on the monitor to let it know that you have started a new cycle. Each morning, check the monitor to see if you need to test that day. If it indicates a test day, test the first urine of the day by putting a fertility test in the stream of your urine. Then insert the test into the monitor. The monitor will tell you if you are not fertile, very fertile or peak fertile.
Here is a link to purchase the Clearblue Fertility Monitor: http://www.amazon.com/Clearblue–Fertility–Monitor–Test–Count/dp/B0000532QB/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&qid=1392854859&sr=8–1&keywords=fertility+monitor"

IVF is the preferred assisted fertility procedure in most fertility clinics. It works by removing several eggs from your ovaries and fertilizing them with your partner’s sperm in a petri dish outside your body. Then the several days old embryo is placed into your uterus in hopes that it will implant. Due to the procedure, the hurdle to getting pregnant is not fertilization but implantation.

Intrauterine insemination (IUI) is one of the simplest of the assisted reproduction methods. It uses a catheter inserted into your vagina to deposit sperm directly into your uterus. Using IUI, your chances of conception is highest when done immediately before or just after ovulation. Your ovulation is determined by a combination of charting your BBT, ovulation prediction kits, and ultrasound. IUI is then done by performing two procedures 24 hours apart.

"You wear an OV Watch on your wrist like a regular watch while you sleep. Around 6 days before ovulation, before your estrogen peaks and LH surges, your chloride icon levels surge. The OV Watch works by taking readings from your skin every 30 minutes to detect the amount of chloride ions on the surface of your skin. It then displays on your watch if you are not fertile, on fertile day 1–4, ovulating, or on the day after ovulation.
Here is a link to purchase an OV Watch: http://www.amazon.com/OV–Watch–Fertility–Predictor–Starter–Sensors/dp/B000K6IQ3W/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&qid=1392857565&sr=8–1&keywords=ov+watch"

Just before ovulation, your body produces a sudden surge or Luteinizing Hormone or LH. OPKs measure the level of LH in your body. So if you have a positive OPK result, it means that you can expect to ovulate within approximately 24 hours of your positive test result. Your Period Tracker Advanced Fertility Chart will color the days that you have a positive test in green.
Once Period Tracker detects that you ovulated, it will forecast your next period start date using your ovulation date + your luteal length.

"Period Tracker normally predicts your next period start date using your average cycle length. For example, if your average cycle length is 28 days, Period Tracker will predict your next period as coming 28 days after the start of your last period.
Predict Periods Using Luteal Length overrides this method of predicting of your next period once Period Tracker has detected that you've ovulated. Once ovulation is detected via the TTC notes that you've inputted, instead of continuing to use your average cycle, it will now predict your next period start date using your ovulation + luteal length. Your luteal length is the number of days that typically pass between your ovulation day and the start of your next period. Using this method once ovulation is detected will likely make your predicted period start date more accurate since luteal length for most women is fairly constant.
By default, Period Tracker sets your luteal length as 14 days. However, you can change your luteal length by going to your app's Settings/General/Ovulation page. Period Tracker will also change your luteal length to more accurately determine your luteal length by using your inputted TTC notes once you have inputted TTC notes for at least one cycle."
